name: Screeching Weasel
label: Lookout!
lede: Ben Weasel and Jughead started a band in the Chicago suburbs in 1986, ended it three times, and wrote the Ramones-and-bubblegum songs a generation of pop-punk bands learned from. Weasel still fronts it.

eras.title: A $200 debut, then the rhythm section leaves
eras.text: Ben Weasel and Jughead start a band in Prospect Heights, work through bassists and drummers, and record on shoestring budgets. In 1989 the rhythm section leaves for a side project and the band stops.

years.h: Two Prospect Heights kids start All Night Garage Sale
years.p: [[Ben Weasel|bdce6736-8bc6-4818-8fd7-781822b674a9]] and Jughead soon settle on Screeching Weasel, with Vinnie Bovine on bass and Steve Cheese on drums.
years.xp: Ben Weasel is Ben Foster and Jughead is John Pierson. Alternative Press describes the two as coworkers when they started.

years.h: A debut recorded in one night for $200
years.p: Screeching Weasel comes out on Underdog Records, with Weasel on vocals and bass and Jughead on guitar. Weasel later disowned it as unrepresentative.
years.xp: Alternative Press describes the songs as brief, crude four-chord punk. The footage here is the band in early 1987, uploaded by Jughead.

years.h: Warren Fischer replaces the fired Vinnie Bovine on bass
years.p: Boogadaboogadaboogada!, on Roadkill Records, is where the band's Ramones-and-bubblegum sound takes shape.
years.xp: Drummer Steve Cheese was also let go, reportedly for refusing to tour beyond Chicago, and [[Aaron Cometbus|47e0c017-6e9e-408b-8c9e-e01950fb4892]] filled in for two shows. Brian Vermin took the drum seat.

years.cap: Flyer for Operation Ivy and Screeching Weasel at 924 Gilman Street, Berkeley, c. 1988
years.h: Opening for Operation Ivy, with Larry Livermore watching
years.p: [[Larry Livermore|427f8569-3791-4887-976c-242bb49a573f]] of Lookout Records catches the band at 924 Gilman Street in Berkeley. He had already offered to put out a record, and the band had turned him down.

years.h: Warren Fischer quits after a rough tour and Dan Vapid takes his bass
years.p: Vapid's first record with the band is the Punkhouse EP on Limited Potential.

years.h: The rhythm section picks Sludgeworth, and the band stops
years.p: Dan Vapid and Brian Vermin choose their side project over Screeching Weasel. Weasel and Jughead form The Gore Gore Girls, and Weasel sings briefly with the first incarnation of [[The Vindictives|553600a9-b0a7-4526-91c5-b8dcff29a895]].

eras.title: A benefit show that wouldn't stay a benefit
eras.text: A one-night gig to pay off old recording debts turns the band into a working one again, with Dan Panic on drums and Dan Vapid writing with Weasel. The result is My Brain Hurts.

years.h: One night in Chicago to pay off old recording debts
years.p: Ben Weasel, Jughead, Dan Vapid, Brian Vermin and Doug Ward reunite for the gig. It goes well enough that they stay together.

years.h: Dan Panic takes the drums as Weasel stops playing guitar
years.p: Weasel decides to concentrate on singing. Dan Sullivan, known as Dan Panic, joins, and Dave Naked plays bass on the next record.

q: Larry Livermore, on his producer credit
years.src: Wikipedia: My Brain Hurts · Alternative Press
years.h: My Brain Hurts goes down in four days in San Francisco
years.p: Recorded July 2, 3, 8 and 9, 1991 at Art of Ears with Andy Ernst and [[Larry Livermore|427f8569-3791-4887-976c-242bb49a573f]], it comes out on Lookout as LK 50.
years.xp:
Livermore said the band had every song worked out in advance, so 14 tracks plus three compilation songs went down in days. Weasel called Dan Vapid the only person he felt comfortable writing with. Jughead's only writing credit is the re-recorded "Fathead."

A dispute nearly sank the deal: "I Wanna Be a Homosexual" had been promised to filmmaker Bruce LaBruce. Weasel also wanted a new band name, but Livermore's contract kept the Screeching Weasel brand.

AllMusic's Mike DaRonco gave the record 4.5 stars and called it an album that would influence "seemingly a million imitators."

years.h: A flat on the way to Gilman Street rides onstage
years.p: On tour behind the Lookout signing, the band blows a tire en route to 924 Gilman Street and hauls the ruined tire onto the stage that night.
years.xp:
Alternative Press recalls the room: "Jesse from Operation Ivy and Jake from Filth spiked their hair and were in the pit."

The video is the band's full set at Gilman on April 10, 1993, from a master VHS.

eras.title: Weasel decides he's done with the stage
eras.text: Wiggle, Anthem for a New Tomorrow and How to Make Enemies and Irritate People arrive on Lookout in two years, with a Ramones cover album on Selfless in between. The lineup keeps shifting, and in 1994 Weasel ends it again.

years.h: Screeching Weasel plays the whole first [[Ramones|d6ed7887-a401-47a8-893c-34b967444d26]] album
years.p: Released on Selfless Records in 1992, it says where Weasel's own sound came from.

years.h: [[Mass Giorgini|abcbcb2a-f783-4300-ba85-3cb1a32c6b2b]] of Squirtgun produces Wiggle
years.p: Scott "Gub" Conway plays bass on the Lookout album, the first the band makes with Giorgini.

years.src: Wikipedia: Anthem for a New Tomorrow
yt: Live on Take No Prisoners TV, 1993
years.h: Weasel writes Anthem for a New Tomorrow as a panic attack
years.p: Recorded at Sonic Iguana in Lafayette, Indiana, with Dan Vapid moving to bass and Weasel on second guitar. Weasel wrote 17 of the 18 songs.
years.xp:
Weasel said he wanted the album to sound "like a panic attack" and has cited Wire's Pink Flag as a template. Vapid co-wrote only "Trance."

Dustin Kensrue of Thrice, speaking in 2022, praised its "lighthearted, weird playfulness" next to serious political ramifications. Mark Rubano of Taking Back Sunday has named it among his formative teenage records.

years.h: Lookout run ends with How to Make Enemies and Irritate People
years.p: Released in 1994, it is the last of the Lookout albums, and Ben Weasel is done with live shows soon after.

years.h: Weasel decides he is done playing live, and the band ends again
years.p: Dan Vapid leaves after a falling out with him. Weasel, Vapid and Dan Panic form The Riverdales, which tour with Green Day.
years.xp: The Riverdales kept the pop-punk going with the same three players.

eras.title: Back on Fat Wreck, then Jughead wants to tour
eras.text: Mass Giorgini joins on bass with a Squirtgun rhythm section behind him, and the band records for Fat Wreck Chords and its own Panic Button label. It ends in 2001 over touring.

years.h: Ben Weasel and Jughead come back on Fat Wreck Chords
years.p: Bark Like a Dog has Giorgini and Dan Lumley of Squirtgun alongside guitarist Zac Damon. Vapid and Dan Panic play on it, then step aside by mutual decision.

years.h: Bark Like a Dog reaches No. 34 on the Heatseekers chart
years.p: It remains the band's highest-charting album.

years.h: The band starts its own label, Panic Button Records
years.p: It releases the Major Label Debut EP in 1998, the same year Television City Dream comes out on Fat Wreck Chords.

years.h: Television City Dream follows Bark Like a Dog to Fat Wreck
years.p: Fat Mike's label puts it out with Damon, Giorgini and Lumley in the lineup.

years.h: Zac Damon sits out Emo for school
years.p: The Panic Button album is recorded by the band as a four-piece.

years.h: Their first shows since 1993 are 30-minute matinees at the House of Blues
years.p: Teen Punks in Heat, out in 2000 on Panic Button, is the last record of this run.

years.h: Jughead is frustrated at the lack of touring, and the band ends
years.p: The July 6, 2001 split is the third, and allegedly the last.

eras.title: Weasel writes books, and the masters come home
eras.text: The band is dormant but the catalog moves: Ben Weasel takes the masters back from Lookout and Asian Man reissues them. Weasel publishes a novel and Jughead forms Even in Blackouts.

years.h: Weasel writes a novel about a fictional punk band
years.p: Like Hell comes with a solo LP, Fidatevi. Jughead forms Even in Blackouts and later writes Weasels in a Box.

years.src: Wikipedia: My Brain Hurts · Wikipedia: Screeching Weasel
years.h: Weasel takes the masters back from Lookout
years.p: After long money and personal conflicts, the catalog is relicensed and reissued by Asian Man Records.
years.xp:
The band plays surprise sets at Chicago's Fireside Bowl with Ben Weasel, Jughead, Dan Vapid, Mass Giorgini and Dan Lumley.

Wikipedia dates the masters in 2004 and also has Weasel leaving Lookout in 2005 over unpaid royalties, so the two years describe the same split.

years.h: My Brain Hurts played start to finish at Reggie's Rock Club
years.p: Weasel and Vapid do two Chicago shows for the album's anniversary.

eras.title: Weasel without Jughead, and a night at SXSW
eras.text: Ben Weasel restarts the band without his co-founder after a legal fight, puts out First World Manifesto, and loses four bandmates after SXSW.

years.big: "I don't recall having kicked myself out of the band."
years.h: Ben Weasel announces a new Screeching Weasel, minus Jughead
years.p: Jughead, on MySpace. Weasel says on his blog that legal issues had kept him from doing his own band on his own terms.
years.xp:
Weasel described the split as the result of a two-year legal fight over band business rather than an amicable parting, and later moved catalog work from Asian Man to Recess Records. Jughead's long MySpace statement said the band was never supposed to exist without both of them.

The new lineup was Weasel, Dan Vapid, guitarist Simon Lamb or Drew Fredrichsen, bassist Justin Perkins and drummer Adam Cargin.

years.cap: Screeching Weasel live, March 2011, the 2009-11 lineup
years.h: After eleven years, First World Manifesto
years.p: Fat Wreck Chords releases it, with Mike Kennerty of The All-American Rejects producing.

years.cap: Ben Weasel singing live during SXSW week, March 2011
years.h: Four bandmates quit after Weasel punches a fan at SXSW
years.p: At Austin's Scoot Inn, Weasel punched a woman who had thrown beer and ice and spat on him. He apologized March 22, and four members resigned March 23.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the Scoot Inn set March 18, 2011. The bandmates announced their exit through a Punknews.org statement.

The 25th anniversary "Weasel Fest" was cancelled March 31, and Fat Mike said in July 2011 he had no interest in releasing another Screeching Weasel record.

eras.title: Never breaking up again
eras.text: A new lineup at Reggie's, a crowd-funded rock opera, a run of records, and Chicago shows that sell out in under an hour in 2025.

years.h: A new lineup opens at Reggie's with The Queers
years.p: Ben Weasel returns with Zac Damon, Dave Klein, Pierre Marche and Mike Hunchback. The Carnival of Schadenfreude EP follows on Recess in November.
years.xp: The EP has seven songs and Mike Kennerty produced it.

years.h: Fans fund Weasel's rock opera Baby Fat: Act 1
years.p: He announces it on YouTube on July 13, 2014, and it raises over $40,000.

years.h: Some Freaks of Atavism counts as studio album number 13
years.p: It comes out March 24, 2020 on Monona Music. The Awful Disclosures of Screeching Weasel follows July 15, 2022, produced by Mike Kennerty, who also joins on guitar.
years.xp: The last shows before the pandemic were in 2019, and COVID postponed tour plans.

years.cap: Live with The Queers, Hobart, Australia, March 30, 2025
yt: Punk in the Park, Cow Palace, May 3, 2025
years.h: Weasel says the band dies when he does, and Chicago sells out
years.p: The March 2025 Chicago shows sell out in under an hour after the pandemic pause. Gianluca Panero joins on guitar.
years.xp: Weasel's line, as Wikipedia prints it: "Screeching Weasel is never breaking up again. The band dies when I do."
